hub.speaker: Former Headman
hub.text: Village's had a bad run. Crops came up wrong two seasons straight, animals spooked for no cause, and the ledger won't add up no matter how many times I recount it. Something's collecting on us, and I mean to know what.

text_variants.text: Whatever you find out there, I want to hear it plain. No riddles, and no half-truths either. The witch keeps to the hollow — west, past my fields, where the trees break.
Whatever you did, the air's changed. I can feel it in my knees, and I trust my knees more than most people.
Word's got round about a fight at the hollow. Briars don't walk off on their own account, whatever spooked them into it worked. I've stopped asking how you people manage these things.
Talked her to terms, they tell me. Didn't figure that witch for a bargaining sort, but the fields don't seem to mind however you settled it.

options.text: You said you don't truck with witches.
Not much of a headman anymore, is there?
Remind me what needs doing about the witch?
That ledger of yours. Still short?
The tally's honest. Somebody's crop failed and they were ashamed of it.
The flood work's done. The count came right in the doing.
Your shortfall had teeth. The granary corner's clear now.

brief.speaker: Former Headman
brief.text: We don't truck with witches here. Didn't used to, anyway. But there's one in the old hollow past the fields, and half the village is pretending not to know it. Crops fail, stock spooks, and one of my own stands there mumbling like her mouth belongs to someone else. Find out what she wants, and end it. However you have to.

witches_topic.speaker: Former Headman
witches_topic.text: We didn't USE to truck with witches, I mean. Things change when the harvest doesn't. Everyone's something these days, I suppose. Even me, apparently, since I sent someone door to door instead of walking out there myself.

reported.speaker: Former Headman
reported.text: Handled. Good. I won't ask how — a man learns when not to ask, running a village long enough. Whatever you did, thank you. Truly.

authority_topic.speaker: Former Headman
authority_topic.text: There's a new authority in Riverfarm proper — a real one, and the village answers to it gladly enough. I mind this end of things the old way. Someone has to know where the shovels are.

favor_recap.speaker: Former Headman
favor_recap.text: The witch keeps to the hollow, west past my own fields, where the trees give out. Whatever she's owed, you'll have to settle it out there.

text_variants.text: Sounds like it's already settled, out at the hollow. Come say so plain, then, so I know to stop chewing on it.

flood_brief.speaker: Former Headman
flood_brief.text: River comes up every spring, and every spring we count what we can carry above the line. This year the count's eleven bushels short and there isn't a thief in this village. That's worse than a thief. Go down to the mill, walk the tally with the tallyman, and bring me an answer I can live with.

flood_reported_read.speaker: Former Headman
flood_reported_read.text: Ashamed. Three seasons of it, and they'd sooner be counted light-fingered than counted unlucky. Then we don't say the name. Eleven bushels off my own share and the ledger balances, and the village can go on thinking whatever keeps it civil.

flood_reported_worked.speaker: Former Headman
flood_reported_worked.text: You did a week of my people's week in a day, and the count came right because somebody finally stood in that shed long enough to see all of it at once. I've been recounting a stack I couldn't see over. I'll take the lesson.

flood_reported_cleared.speaker: Former Headman
flood_reported_cleared.text: Teeth. Eleven bushels of teeth. I'd rather it was vermin than a neighbour and I'm not proud of that either. Take something off the field board, and don't tell me what you found down there again.
